_readme: Evaluation set covering 5 documents of different types, indexed together: a resume (PDF), a career/salary analysis (XLSX), a conference presentation (PPTX), a dataset-analysis report (DOCX), and an academic paper (PDF). Every expected_keywords entry was verified by hand against the actual parsed chunk text on 2026-09-22 (not guessed) -- see backend/eval/README.md for how. Still a seed set, not a finished benchmark: 36 questions is short of the 50+ target, all documents are from one person's personal/academic files (no contracts, legal docs, or genuinely adversarial content), and the XLSX questions deliberately avoid specific numbers because Docling's table-structure model is disabled by default in this project (see settings.DOCLING_DO_TABLE_STRUCTURE) and its markdown table export sometimes misaligns columns -- a good illustration of why that's a real, documented limitation and not just a settings toggle nobody will notice. Each item's category is 'factual' (answerable from the indexed document(s)) or 'unanswerable' (deliberately out of scope, to test the refusal path).

items.question: What is this person's name?
What degree is this person pursuing and at which institute?
What internship did this person do at Authenta.ai?
What did this person do during their internship at Inadev Pvt. Ltd.?
What programming languages are listed under technical skills?
What machine learning frameworks or libraries does this person know?
What is the QuantEdge Investment Advisor project about?
What certifications does this person have?
What achievements or awards are listed?
What position of responsibility did this person hold in the Coding Ninjas Club?
What database technologies are mentioned in the skills section?
What cloud or DevOps tools does this person list?
What is the capital of France?
items.notes: Not in the document at all -- must trigger the refusal path, not a hallucinated fact.

items.question: What was this person's salary at their internship?
items.notes: Plausible-sounding but not present in a resume -- checks the system doesn't invent numbers.

items.question: Summarize this person's PhD thesis.
items.notes: Presupposes something false (a PhD thesis) -- checks the system doesn't play along with a false premise.
